problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -16\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of a Span

feedback.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ ${a}_{3},$ and ${a}_{4}$ are given below. Determine whether $B={{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3},$ where ${a}_{4}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+{x}_{3}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-4 \\ -9{x}_{1}-8{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -4 \\ -9 & 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -15 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-15,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=17,$ meaning that

$$
(-15)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+0\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+17\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=(-15)+0+17=2.$
